title: AI API Failure Triage
summary: Classify authentication, request, quota, timeout, rate-limit, provider, and application failures before retrying or escalating an AI API call.
prerequisites: Access to redacted request metadata and application telemetry
A documented timeout and retry budget
Provider status and support paths for the deployed service

sections.title: Classify the failing boundary
paragraphs: Confirm the exact application, provider, endpoint or API version, model, region, timestamp, attempt, timeout, and request identifier. Separate DNS or connection failure, authentication, authorization, malformed request, unavailable resource, content or safety stop, context limit, quota, rate limit, provider overload, application parsing, and downstream side effects. A provider HTTP response proves connectivity, not end-to-end success.

Do not retry authentication, permission, invalid-request, unsupported-model, or deterministic application-validation failures unchanged. Retry only a classified transient failure within one total budget that includes SDK retries, proxy retries, and application retries. Apply jitter, honor provider guidance, cap concurrency, and preserve an operation ID so a repeated call cannot duplicate a downstream action.

sections.title: Record a privacy-safe API triage packet
paragraphs: Capture headers and identifiers needed for support while excluding credentials, full prompts, user content, and unrestricted model output. Compare a minimal synthetic request from the same deployment path; do not use a successful request from a different region, account, API surface, or model as proof that the affected boundary is healthy.

code.label: AI API failure record
code.code:
Service and operation: [PROVIDER/API/MODEL -> APPLICATION OPERATION ID]
Version and environment: [APP/PROMPT/SDK/API/REGION]
Timestamp and correlation: [UTC -> REQUEST/RESPONSE/TRACE IDS]
Observed failure: [HTTP/STATUS/ERROR/STOP REASON]
Failure class: [NETWORK | AUTH | INVALID | LIMIT | SAFETY | CONTEXT | PROVIDER | APP | DOWNSTREAM]
Sensitive-data review: [REDACTED FIELDS -> AUTHORIZED EVIDENCE]
Total retry budget: [SDK + PROXY + APP -> ATTEMPT/LIMIT]
Minimal synthetic reproduction: [RESULT]
Owner and cadence: [ON-CALL ROLE -> UPDATE INTERVAL]
Stop criteria: [NON-TRANSIENT | BUDGET | COST | SAFETY | UNKNOWN SIDE EFFECT]
Recovery or escalation: [DEGRADE | FAIL CLOSED | RESTORE CONFIG | PROVIDER CASE]
Verification: [USER JOURNEY, POSTCONDITION, AND ERROR RATE]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the classified failure, redacted correlation identifiers, effective configuration, total attempts, minimal reproduction, provider or dependency state, containment decision, and an owner. Verify recovery with the affected route and model, a representative request, application parsing, latency and error-rate observation, and any downstream postcondition.

Stop retries when the failure is non-transient, the shared budget is exhausted, costs or load exceed the boundary, a safety control fires, provider guidance says not to retry, or a prior request may already have caused a side effect. Recovery means reducing load or failing safely, restoring the last verified configuration when a change caused the issue, reconciling uncertain operations, and escalating persistent provider failures with redacted IDs and a timeline.
sections.callout: Retry is a controlled response to a transient class, not a default response to every error.

sections.title: Scope, evidence, and offline simulation boundary
paragraphs: This practical preserves the provider-neutral investigation scope: classify the failing boundary, record privacy-safe evidence, make a bounded retry decision, and verify recovery independently. Every case is an authored, fictional normalized application record evaluated offline. The lab does not call a provider, inspect a live account, use a secret, spend money, sleep, mutate production, grant approval, or demonstrate current provider health or successful production recovery.

The normalized fields are application fields, not DeepSeek or Mistral wire envelopes. A provider HTTP response proves that transport reached an HTTP response, but it does not prove end-to-end application success. HTTP 200 can still be followed by a parsing failure or a safety stop. Conversely, a missing transport observation does not establish the terminal outcome of an operation. If a local timeout follows a request that may have caused a downstream action, the side-effect state is unknown and the operation must not be blindly restarted.

DeepSeek documents 400 as a malformed body, 401 as a wrong key, 402 as insufficient balance, 422 as invalid parameters, 429 as excessive request pace, 500 as a server issue, and 503 as overload. Its page recommends waiting and retrying for applicable server and overload cases: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/error_codes. These narrow distinctions do not establish a response envelope, exact retry delay, SDK default, quota, idempotency guarantee, or live capability. Under this application policy, an unchanged DeepSeek 402 is classified as LIMIT but is not retried.

Mistral lists 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504. It identifies 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 as transient and recommends exponential backoff: https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/error-glossary. That guidance does not override unknown side effects, safety controls, application budgets, or deadlines, and it does not establish an exact SDK retry count or idempotency guarantee.

The application vocabulary is NETWORK for absent transport or connection failure, AUTH for authentication or permission, INVALID for malformed or unsupported input, LIMIT for quota, balance, or pacing limits, SAFETY for a safety stop, CONTEXT for a context limit, PROVIDER for a provider-side transient, APP for application validation or parsing, and DOWNSTREAM for a side-effect or postcondition failure. The executable policy supports only the explicit provider and status combinations represented in its compatibility map. Unsupported combinations are rejected rather than guessed. Provider documentation supports the cited status meanings, while the retry gates, fixture values, thresholds, and normalized error codes are supplied application policy.

sections.title: Exact investigation and retry-decision procedure
paragraphs: 1. Freeze and redact the evidence. Record provider, service, operation, route, endpoint version, model, region, environment, UTC timestamp, correlation ID, application operation ID, provider request ID or the literal UNKNOWN, transport observation, HTTP status, normalized error code, and effective configuration. Remove credentials, authorization headers, full prompts, user content, and unrestricted output.

2. Count every actual outbound attempt exactly once across SDK, proxy, and application layers. attempts_performed is completed work. total_attempt_budget is the maximum completed outbound attempts allowed for the operation. RETRY authorizes one next outbound attempt; it is not a persistent reservation. It is allowed only when attempts_performed is less than total_attempt_budget. The budget is shared, not multiplied by three layers. A real caller must atomically record and consume the shared budget before dispatch. Otherwise, repeated evaluation of the decision could spend the same authorization twice.

3. Validate before deciding. Reject missing or empty identifiers, unsupported providers, unsupported provider/status/class combinations, malformed normalized error codes, status and error-code disagreement, Boolean values used as numbers, non-finite or negative limits, nonpositive attempt timeouts, jitter outside its declared bounds, attempts above budget, elapsed time above deadline, contradictory transport/status observations, inconsistent safety flags, and contradictory effective-configuration values. Numeric conversion failures, including overflow while checking extremely large integers, are normalized to ValueError.

4. The effective configuration must have exactly these keys: shared_attempt_budget, sdk_retries_counted, proxy_retries_counted, application_retries_counted, exponential_indexing, max_delay_scope, and jitter_source. shared_attempt_budget must be a strict non-Boolean integer equal to total_attempt_budget. All three counted flags must be true. The indexing, cap scope, and jitter values must be the supported semantics named by the fixture. A validator must reject contradictions rather than silently overriding them.

5. Separate observation from outcome. transport_observed false requires a null HTTP status and NETWORK classification in this lab. A provider response requires transport_observed true. side_effect_state none means the supplied evidence says no side effect occurred, complete means the postcondition is confirmed, and unknown means the outcome is unresolved. Both complete and unknown stop another attempt.

6. Apply gates in this order: stop for complete side effect; stop for unknown side effect; stop for SAFETY; stop for a non-transient class; stop an unchanged DeepSeek 402; stop if the shared attempt budget is exhausted; stop if next_attempt_cost exceeds remaining_cost_budget; compute delay; then stop if delay plus one strictly positive attempt_timeout_seconds reservation exceeds the remaining deadline. A retryable status cannot override any earlier gate.

7. This application policy uses explicit one-based failure indexing. The first already-performed attempt uses exponent zero. The exponent is max(attempts_performed minus 1, 0). The exponential component is min(max_delay_seconds, backoff_base_seconds multiplied by 2 to that exponent). max_delay_seconds caps only the exponential component. The final delay is max(minimum_delay_seconds, exponential component) plus deterministic_jitter. Therefore a provider or policy minimum can exceed max_delay_seconds and is never shortened, and jitter can make the final delay exceed max_delay_seconds while remaining inside its declared bounds. The bounded calculation uses log2 and ldexp to avoid constructing an unbounded power. Python's math.isfinite rejects non-finite values, while extreme numeric operations are converted into validation errors.

8. Compute remaining deadline as deadline_seconds minus elapsed_seconds. RETRY is returned only if the final delay plus attempt_timeout_seconds is less than or equal to the remaining deadline. The program returns a zero delay with STOP because no retry is authorized, while its trace retains the proposed delay and remaining-deadline arithmetic for diagnosis. It performs no real sleep. RETRY authorizes one attempt only. It does not itself atomically reserve or consume that attempt.

9. After containment, verify recovery separately. Require the same route and model, a representative request through the named boundary, successful application parsing, raw quality and error numerators and denominators over a named UTC observation window, raw latency samples and supplied thresholds, and a confirmed downstream postcondition. Parse explicit UTC start and end ISO timestamps. Missing, malformed, non-UTC, reversed, or equal windows return UNKNOWN. Malformed numeric evidence, including NaN, infinity, and numeric overflow, also returns UNKNOWN. Do not infer recovery from an assertion, HTTP 200, or a retry decision alone.

10. layer_counts is only a fictional fixture default used to make complete records: the first attempt is assigned to SDK, the second to proxy, and the remainder to application. It is not inferred real attribution. Explicit nonnegative SDK, proxy, and application distributions that sum to attempts_performed are accepted.

sections.title: Complete worked fictional inputs and traceable results
paragraphs: All nine records are fictional normalized application records, not vendor responses. Their common completed fields are: service ai-gateway; operation generate_answer; route /v1/answer; endpoint_version normalized-v1; model redacted-model; region test-region-1; environment offline-lab; timestamp 2026-09-20T10:15:00Z; nonempty case-specific correlation, operation, and provider request IDs; total attempt budget 3; deadline 20.0 seconds; elapsed 1.0 second; attempt timeout 1.0 second; backoff base 0.0 seconds; exponential cap 30.0 seconds; minimum delay 0.0 seconds; jitter bounds 0.0 through 0.0; deterministic jitter 0.0; next-attempt cost 0.4 units; remaining cost budget 1.0 unit; safety false; side-effect state none. The redacted effective configuration explicitly says SDK, proxy, and application attempts share one total, the exponential cap applies before the minimum floor and jitter, and deterministic jitter is injected. The sensitive-data review says secrets, prompts, user content, authorization, and unrestricted output were removed. Reproduction, ownership, stop criteria, escalation path, and verification requirements are populated by the fixture builder.

Case 1, bad authentication: DeepSeek; transport observed; HTTP 401; normalized error code 401; AUTH; attempts by layer SDK 1, proxy 0, application 0; attempts performed 1; IDs corr-auth, op-auth, and req-auth. Completed result: STOP, NON_TRANSIENT_AUTH, zero reserved attempts, returned delay 0.00. Retrying the unchanged key cannot correct authentication.

Case 2, invalid request: DeepSeek; transport observed; HTTP 422; normalized error code 422; INVALID; one SDK attempt; IDs corr-invalid, op-invalid, and req-invalid. Completed result: STOP, NON_TRANSIENT_INVALID, zero reserved attempts, returned delay 0.00. The parameters must be corrected first.

Case 3, insufficient balance: DeepSeek; transport observed; HTTP 402; normalized error code 402; LIMIT; one SDK attempt; IDs corr-balance, op-balance, and req-balance. Completed result: STOP, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, zero reserved attempts, returned delay 0.00. An unchanged balance failure is not retried.

Case 4, throttling: Mistral; transport observed; HTTP 429; normalized error code 429; LIMIT; one SDK attempt; backoff base 2.0; exponential cap 30.0; minimum delay 2.0; jitter bounds 0.25 through 0.75; injected jitter 0.50; IDs corr-throttle, op-throttle, and req-throttle. One performed attempt means exponent max(1 minus 1, 0) = 0. The exponential component is min(30.0, 2.0 times 2^0) = 2.0. The floor remains 2.0 and jitter gives 2.50. Remaining deadline is 19.00; 2.50 delay plus 1.00 attempt timeout is 3.50, which fits. Completed result: RETRY, TRANSIENT_WITHIN_BUDGET, one reserved attempt, delay 2.50.

Case 5, server transient: DeepSeek; transport observed; HTTP 503; normalized error code 503; PROVIDER; layer attempts SDK 1, proxy 1, application 0; attempts performed 2; deadline 10.0; elapsed 3.0; backoff base 0.5; exponential cap 1.0; minimum delay 1.0; jitter bounds 0.0 through 0.5; injected jitter 0.25; IDs corr-server, op-server, and req-server. Exponent max(2 minus 1, 0) = 1. The exponential component is min(1.0, 0.5 times 2^1) = 1.0. The floor remains 1.0 and jitter gives 1.25. Remaining deadline is 7.00; 1.25 plus 1.00 is 2.25, which fits. Completed result: RETRY, TRANSIENT_WITHIN_BUDGET, one reserved attempt, delay 1.25.

Case 6, throttling after an exhausted shared budget: Mistral; HTTP 429; normalized error code 429; LIMIT; attempts by layer SDK 1, proxy 1, application 1; attempts performed 3; total budget 3; IDs corr-exhausted, op-exhausted, and req-exhausted. Completed result: STOP, ATTEMPT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, zero reserved attempts, delay 0.00. No hidden per-layer multiplier exists.

Case 7, local timeout after possible downstream action: Synthetic; transport not observed; HTTP status null; normalized error code TRANSPORT_UNKNOWN; NETWORK; one SDK attempt; provider request ID UNKNOWN; side-effect state unknown; IDs corr-unknown and op-unknown. Completed result: STOP, UNKNOWN_SIDE_EFFECT, zero reserved attempts, delay 0.00. The missing transport observation is not a terminal outcome, so reconciliation must precede any restart.

Case 8, safety stop after HTTP 200: Synthetic; transport observed; HTTP 200; normalized error code SAFETY_STOP; SAFETY; safety flag true; one SDK attempt; IDs corr-safety, op-safety, and req-safety. Completed result: STOP, SAFETY_CONTROL, zero reserved attempts, delay 0.00. HTTP 200 does not override the safety result.

Case 9, parsing failure after HTTP 200: Synthetic; transport observed; HTTP 200; normalized error code PARSE_ERROR; APP; safety false; one SDK attempt; IDs corr-parse, op-parse, and req-parse. Completed result: STOP, NON_TRANSIENT_APP, zero reserved attempts, delay 0.00. The response was observed, but end-to-end application success was not achieved.

sections.title: Complete Python 3 standard-library offline lab
paragraphs: Save this complete file as api_failure_lab.py. It uses only the Python standard library, makes no network request, performs no sleep, reads no secret, makes no paid call, and mutates no production system. The fixture builder supplies complete normalized records, all nine worked cases, the independent changed-input task, the recovery fixture, and regression tests.

The normalized error code is required and checked for type and provider/status consistency. Effective configuration values are checked, not merely their keys. The recovery verifier checks the named UTC window before computing metrics. The fictional layer distribution is a fixture convenience only, not a claim about actual SDK, proxy, or application attribution.

code.label: api_failure_lab.py

sections.title: Independent changed-input task
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the feedback and causal key. Use the callable assigned_task_fixture in the file or construct the same complete normalized record yourself. The changed record is DeepSeek; service ai-gateway; operation generate_answer; route /v1/answer; endpoint normalized-v1; model redacted-model; offline-lab environment; nonempty IDs corr-assigned, op-assigned, and req-assigned; transport observed true; HTTP 500; normalized error code 500; PROVIDER; attempts by layer SDK 1, proxy 1, application 0; attempts performed 2; total attempt budget 3; elapsed 9.5 seconds; deadline 10.0 seconds; positive attempt timeout 0.1 second; backoff base 0.5 second; exponential cap 30.0 seconds; minimum delay 1.0 second; jitter bounds 0.0 through 0.2 second; deterministic jitter 0.1 second; next-attempt cost 0.4 unit; remaining cost budget 1.0 unit; safety false; side-effect state none. Retain the complete redacted configuration and evidence fields supplied by the builder.

Without making a live call, calculate the normalized class, attempts already performed, nominal attempts left, exponent, capped exponential component, effective floor, jittered proposed delay, remaining deadline, positive attempt-time reservation, final decision, reason, reserved attempts, and returned delay. State why the HTTP response does not itself prove end-to-end success.

Then list what would be required to verify a real recovery: the affected route and model, effective configuration, a representative request through the same boundary, application parsing, raw quality and error counts over a named observation window, raw latency samples against a supplied threshold, and the downstream postcondition. Do not inspect the next section until you have recorded your answer.

sections.title: Separate feedback and causal key
paragraphs: Specific feedback: selecting RETRY merely because DeepSeek documents a 500 server issue as a wait-and-retry case misses the application deadline gate. A provider distinction identifies a potentially transient class, but it does not authorize an attempt outside the total application budget. Conversely, selecting STOP because the attempt budget or cost is exhausted identifies the wrong cause here. Two attempts are below the total budget of three, and 0.4 cost units fit within the remaining 1.0 unit.

Causal key: the class is PROVIDER. Two actual attempts have already been counted, leaving one nominal attempt. The one-based failure index gives exponent max(2 minus 1, 0) = 1. The exponential component is min(30.0, 0.5 times 2^1) = 1.0 second. The minimum floor is 1.0 second and is not shortened. Adding 0.1 second of injected jitter gives a proposed delay of 1.1 seconds. The remaining deadline is 10.0 minus 9.5 = 0.5 second. The retry would require 1.1 seconds of delay plus the positive 0.1-second attempt-timeout reservation, totaling 1.2 seconds. Since 1.2 is greater than 0.5, the exact decision is STOP, reason DEADLINE, reserved attempts 0, returned delay 0.00. The diagnostic trace retains proposed_delay 1.1 and remaining 0.5.

The observed HTTP 500 establishes that an HTTP response was observed in this fictional normalized record. It does not prove successful parsing, an acceptable user result, or a completed downstream postcondition. A strong recovery answer requires the same /v1/answer route and redacted-model, the effective configuration, a representative same-boundary request, successful parsing, raw quality and error numerators and denominators over a named window, latency samples evaluated against a supplied threshold, and a confirmed downstream postcondition. Missing required evidence yields UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Exact command, expected stdout, and observed fixture arithmetic
paragraphs: Run the offline file with the exact command python3 api_failure_lab.py. No package installation is required. The program performs no network request and no sleep. Its main stdout remains exactly the v3 transcript below. The regression suite now includes the concrete configuration, UTC-window, NaN, infinity, and extreme-integer defects while retaining the existing invalid and valid outcomes; its displayed count remains the established fixture count of 22 grouped regression checks.

Cases 1 through 3 stop for authentication, invalid input, and insufficient balance. Case 4 uses exponent zero and returns 2.50. Case 5 uses exponent one and returns 1.25. Case 6 proves that three completed attempts exhaust one shared budget of three. Cases 7 through 9 distinguish unknown outcome, safety after HTTP 200, and parsing failure after HTTP 200.

The recovery line evaluates only the authored fixture. Its error rate is 1 divided by 200, or 0.005, against a supplied maximum of 0.01. Its maximum latency is 1.60 seconds from samples 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6, against a supplied maximum of 2.0 seconds. Its quality rate is 19 divided by 20, or 0.950, against a supplied minimum of 0.90. Parsing, same-boundary representation, and the downstream postcondition are explicitly true. This demonstrates an independently evaluable RECOVERED result for an offline fixture, not production recovery or provider health.

The final line is the actual assigned DeepSeek 500 changed-input probe. Its STOP result and zero returned delay match the separate causal key. A matching transcript shows only agreement between the local function, policy, and authored records. RETRY values in this lab authorize one attempt; a production caller must atomically record and consume that shared attempt before dispatch to prevent duplicate budget spending.

sections.title: Completed escalation packet and independent recovery evidence
paragraphs: Completed fictional offline escalation packet: provider Synthetic; service ai-gateway; operation generate_answer; route /v1/answer; endpoint normalized-v1; model redacted-model; region test-region-1; environment offline-lab; timestamp 2026-09-20T10:15:00Z; correlation ID corr-unknown; application operation ID op-unknown; provider request ID UNKNOWN; transport observed false; HTTP status null; normalized error code TRANSPORT_UNKNOWN; class NETWORK; attempts by layer SDK 1, proxy 0, application 0; attempts performed 1; total budget 3; deadline 20.0 seconds; elapsed 1.0 second; positive attempt timeout 1.0 second; next cost 0.4 unit; remaining cost 1.0 unit; safety false; side-effect state unknown. Decision: STOP, UNKNOWN_SIDE_EFFECT, with no reserved attempt.

Its effective configuration is redacted but explicit: SDK, proxy, and application attempts count toward one shared budget; the first performed attempt uses exponent zero; max delay caps only the exponential component; the minimum floor is never shortened; jitter is deterministic fixture input. Removed data includes secrets, prompts, user content, authorization, and unrestricted output. Retained evidence includes route, model label, deployment boundary, operation and correlation IDs, timing, normalized observation, and permitted application logs.

Containment owner is the application on-call role. The fictional packet specifies a 15-minute update cadence for an actual incident, but this is not a live incident schedule or approval. Stop criteria are complete or unknown side effect, safety, non-transient classification, insufficient balance, exhausted shared attempts, cost cap, and insufficient deadline. The recovery path is to reconcile the operation through a safe read when available, fail closed if reconciliation is unavailable, and escalate persistent provider issues with redacted IDs and a timeline. No provider-specific idempotency property is assumed.

The separate recovery fixture records a successful application observation rather than disguising success as an APP failure. It contains provider Mistral; service ai-gateway; route /v1/answer; model redacted-model; redacted effective configuration ID; environment offline-lab; operation ID op-recovery-01; correlation ID corr-recovery-01; provider request ID req-recovery-01; a representative same-boundary request; successful application parsing; named window 2026-09-20T10:20:00Z through 2026-09-20T10:25:00Z; 1 error among 200 requests; latency samples 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6 seconds; 19 quality passes among 20 samples; confirmed downstream postcondition; maximum error rate 0.01; maximum latency 2.0 seconds; and minimum quality rate 0.90.

The verifier computes 0.005 error rate, 1.60-second maximum latency, and 0.950 quality rate. With all required evidence present and thresholds satisfied, it returns RECOVERED for that fictional offline fixture. Removing the latency samples makes the same verifier return UNKNOWN. Complete evidence that fails a supplied threshold returns NOT_RECOVERED. These labels do not establish live provider behavior, production health, approval, legal compliance, or a successful production recovery.

Exact provider wire fields, Retry-After behavior, SDK defaults, account quotas, balance amounts, idempotency guarantees, live capabilities, and current health remain UNKNOWN here. Establishing them would require the deployed provider documentation, SDK version, account configuration, and authorized telemetry. The cited provider pages are used only for their narrow documented error distinctions and general retry guidance.
